body:
An AI receptionist in Denton, Texas answers your business calls 24/7 in a natural voice, books appointments and texts you a summary of each call, in English and Spanish. Texas WebCoders sets one up for Denton, TX businesses from $149/month plus a $299 one-time setup, and most go live in 7 to 14 days. Denton is a college city with two universities, a lively square and a young customer base.

Why Denton businesses miss calls

Denton is home to the University of North Texas and Texas Woman’s University, so a large part of its customer base is young and prefers quick answers. Calls and bookings swing with the academic calendar, especially at move-in, graduation and summer break. Food and entertainment employ about one in nine workers, and independent shops around the Courthouse Square often have one person doing everything.

Which Denton businesses benefit most?

  • Restaurants: Answer hours and table questions while the room is full.
  • Real estate agents: Student leasing seasons create short, intense call spikes.
  • Auto repair shops: Book visits for students and commuters on I-35.

What a call could sound like in Denton

Here is an example of how a call might go. Your script, rules and wording would be set up with you.

Caller: Do you have any two-bedrooms open for August?

AI receptionist: Shares the details you approve, books a tour and sends you the lead.

Does your Denton AI receptionist need Spanish?

About 16.8% of Denton residents age 5 and older speak Spanish at home. About one in six residents speaks Spanish at home, so a bilingual setup is useful, especially for health, legal and home services. Our AI calling agents and AI receptionists speak English and Spanish, and you can read more on our bilingual AI calling agent page.

Can you keep your Denton phone number?

Yes. Denton callers will usually see the 940 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Forward it to the AI for all calls, only after hours, or only when your team does not pick up. We can also set up a new local number. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
